newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses driven down sharply by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses driven down sharply by Wall St.

text.p: An unexpected fall on Wall Street overnight knocked European stocks from their record levels on Friday, igniting fears that the global bull run might be nearing an end.
On currency markets, the dollar, which hit a 47-month high of 120 yen in Asia, weakened in Europe amid rumours of Bank of Japan intervention.

Major European bourses tumbled over one percent in a dramatic reversal after closing at fresh peaks on Thursday when favourable currency movements boosted prospects for exporters. London, Frankfurt and Paris sank further after the early, hefty losses suffered as trading screens flashed up overnight news of New York's retreat late on Thursday which pushed the Dow Jones average off its peaks.

The Dow closed down 94.28 points at 6,755.75 after showing big gains at the London close on Thursday. It was dragged lower by waves of sell programs, apparently triggered by negative sentiment in the futures markets.
London took fright, falling by 1.07 percent from its record close. Supermarket stocks also dropped after J Sainsbury warned that its profits would be well below levels analysts had been predicting.
Though every stock in the FTSE 100 blue chip index was marked lower at one point, some traders were reluctant to call an end to the New Year rally.
"So far anyone that has called the peak has been trampled on," said one head of equity sales. "There have been no prizes for standing in the market's way and saying it has changed direction."
"There have been concerns for some time that the markets have been getting a bit frothy but the trouble is there is so much cash out there," said another trader.

Thursday's spurt in London was driven by belief that sterling's recent strength had ended because British interest rates were unlikely to rise soon. A fall in the pound boosted prospects for overseas-earning sectors.
Frankfurt suffered the biggest drop, falling 1.17 percent on the DAX index in sympathy with Wall Street but many dealers said it was not the large-scale correction many had feared.
"This is not a catastrophe," said one dealer. "It's being seen by some as an opportunity to buy," she noted, adding that it was likely the market would now remain within a tight range.
French shares also fell steeply as investors, with a nervous eye on Wall Street's performance, took profits.
"I do not see any reason for people to panic. We have had quite a run. It all went up very quickly, and it is now time to pause and take profits," a broker said.
On Thursday, French shares closed at a record of 2,461.25 points on the CAC-40 index, which has risen from 2,193.70 on December 17.
On currency markets, the dollar put on a volatile showing. It fell in European trade after leaping above 120 yen overnight in Asia amid a spate of contradictory Japanese comments.
The U.S. currency made the long-awaited rally above the key 120-yen level after official Japanese comments that a weak yen was not greatly damaging the economy.
Dealers saw the remarks as giving a green light to carry the dollar higher and pushed the currency to 120.15 yen, its highest in 47 months.
But later comments by an official from Japan's finance ministry (MOF) that an excessively weak yen was not welcome dragged the dollar down.
Rumours that the Bank of Japan might have sold dollars for yen also helped put an end to the dollar's rally, traders said.
"The market is clearly nervous about the comments coming out of Japan, but it also wants to see the dollar go higher," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro.
CURRENCIES AT 1215 GMT
The dollar was at 118.80 yen and 1.6301 marks from Thursday's late European levels of 119.50 and 1.6380.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1215 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 47.2 points at 4,224.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 26.11 lower at 2,435.14.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 33.19 at 3,000.27.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at higher at $352.95 an ounce, compared to Thursday's close at $349.45. Silver was at $4.96, up seven cents.
